tells.1: Forced folksy opener ('Well, this honey season has certainly kept us on our toes') plus the em-dash closer. The welcome line comes oddly at the end.
tells.3: Redundant reassurance ('you're not alone. Most of us are in the same boat'), and the welcome comes awkwardly at the end.
tells.4: Stacked pleasantries ('We're glad to have you along') and a non-sequitur closer linking winter preparations to hearing about the season.
tells.5: Formulaic closer 'Wherever you are with your winter preparations, we'd love to hear…' that doesn't quite follow.
tells.6: Tidy rule-of-three phrasing ('put the kettle on, catch your breath and enjoy'; 'Bring your questions, brush up… and catch up').

reason: Version 2 is the cleanest and most natural. It welcomes readers up front, gives the workshop and fondant details plainly, and ends simply without stacked pleasantries or a contrived closing line.
